analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/developer/build.md adds a 'Nemotron Super component qualification' section at head lines 253-259. docs/developer/test.md adds the same section plus prompt-golden and image-fixture guidance, head lines 558-576. I found no executable code, workflow, or trust-boundary change. The threat model is not affected: TB-002 and TB-011 and T-052..T-058 are not touched. The text says tiny fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider, MTP speed or full image support, which is consistent with the existing statements that compilation or fixtures do not equal qualification. It adds no claim of production activation or Apple attestation. It references the unchanged-in-this-PR files scripts/nemotron-qualification/README.md, prompt_golden.py, image-goldens, docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md, and the NEMOTRON_SUPER_REFERENCE_DIR env var. None of these were supplied, so their contents (for example, download or checksum handling in the 88-shard verifier and the image decoders, which are attack surface for untrusted media) were not reviewed. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem. Integration should check whether the PR's other files include those scripts or the image decoding code and review them for checksum integrity, bounded decoding, and safe handling of temporary files (compare T-050).
